skill.name: accessibility-compliance-accessibility-audit

content.value_statement: Accessibility barriers expose users and teams to exclusion and compliance risk. This skill guides WCAG audits, test planning, remediation, and evidence-ready reports.
actual_capabilities: Plans audit scope across platforms, WCAG levels, pages, and user journeys.
Guides automated testing with axe-core, jest-axe, pa11y, and CI examples.
Defines manual checks for keyboard, screen reader, contrast, reflow, and cognitive accessibility.
Maps issues to WCAG criteria, severity, user impact, and remediation steps.
Provides accessible component and report patterns for teams to adapt.
limitations: Requires access to the UI, design artifacts, content, or test environment.
Automated scans cannot replace manual assistive technology testing.
Generated guidance must be validated in the target product and legal context.
Does not certify compliance by itself.

use_cases.title: Product Accessibility Audit
use_cases.description: Audit important pages and flows against WCAG criteria, then prioritize barriers by user impact and remediation effort.

use_cases.title: Developer Remediation Sprint
use_cases.description: Convert audit findings into practical fixes for labels, keyboard access, focus order, contrast, and semantic structure.

use_cases.title: Compliance Evidence Review
use_cases.description: Prepare clear accessibility evidence, test results, and open risks for stakeholders before release or procurement review.

prompt_templates.title: Start an Audit
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with scope and a simple test plan.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit these pages for WCAG 2.2 AA. Confirm scope first, then list automated and manual checks I should run.

prompt_templates.title: Review Findings
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these accessibility findings. Group them by WCAG criterion, severity, user impact, and remediation priority.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Remediation
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a remediation plan for keyboard, screen reader, contrast, and form-label issues across this product flow.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Program
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an accessibility testing program with CI checks, manual test cadence, evidence capture, and release gates for a multi-team product.

output_examples.input: Audit a checkout flow for WCAG AA.
output: Scope confirmation for pages, browsers, assistive technologies, and target WCAG level.
Prioritized findings with severity, user impact, WCAG mapping, and recommended fixes.
Retest checklist covering keyboard navigation, focus order, contrast, labels, and error handling.

output_examples.input: Review accessibility issues from automated scans.
output: Grouped issue summary that separates critical blockers from lower-priority improvements.
Manual verification steps for issues that automated tools cannot prove.
Clear remediation notes for design, content, and engineering owners.
Recommended automated checks for pull requests and builds.
Manual test cadence for key journeys and assistive technology coverage.
Evidence package outline for stakeholder and compliance review.

best_practices: Define WCAG version, conformance level, pages, journeys, and assistive technology targets before testing.
Combine automated scans with keyboard, screen reader, contrast, reflow, and cognitive checks.
Retest every fix and preserve evidence for compliance reviews.
anti_patterns: Relying only on automated tools for compliance decisions.
Reporting issues without user impact, WCAG criteria, severity, or fix guidance.
Treating sample code as production-ready without adapting it to the target stack.

faq.question: Does this skill guarantee WCAG compliance?
faq.answer: No. It guides testing and remediation, but final compliance depends on product context, validation, and expert review.

faq.question: Which accessibility standards does it support?
faq.answer: It focuses on WCAG-oriented audits, with prompts that can target specific versions and conformance levels.

faq.question: Can it replace manual screen reader testing?
faq.answer: No. It helps plan manual checks, but real assistive technology testing remains necessary.

faq.question: What inputs improve the audit?
faq.answer: Provide target pages, user journeys, WCAG level, known constraints, design files, scan results, and product context.

faq.question: Can developers use it during implementation?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes remediation patterns for keyboard access, labels, focus behavior, contrast, and accessible components.

faq.question: Does it include continuous testing guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes CI guidance, automated scan ideas, manual test cadence, and evidence capture practices.
